title: feat(cli,plugin-dev): an app that declares its own sys_organization default record page boots under os serve and DevPlugin; the conflict remedy names a page, not a package
body:
Fixes #23310
Clause-②: yes

## What this does

Ruling A on #23015 (record `6134056653`) allows one `isDefault: true` record page per object per deployment. PR #23309 added `AuthPluginOptions.registerOrganizationRecordPage` so a host that ships its own `sys_organization` default can leave out `plugin-auth`'s `sys_organization_detail`. The two composition roots that construct `AuthPlugin` themselves, `os serve` and `DevPlugin`, never passed the option. An app served by either one that ships its own `sys_organization` default was refused at boot with `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT`, and the app had no switch to set.

- **Derived, not forwarded.** Both roots now read the served app's own pages before they construct `AuthPlugin`. If the app declares an `isDefault: true` record page for `sys_organization`, they pass `registerOrganizationRecordPage: false`. Otherwise they pass `true`, which is today's behaviour. There is no new stack-config key: the page the author already wrote is the switch.
- **One predicate, two callers.** `stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(stack, plugins?)` is a new export of `@objectstack/core` (`packages/core/src/stack-organization-record-page.ts`). `serve.ts` calls it with `(config, plugins)` and `dev-plugin.ts` with `(this.options.stack)`. It reads `pages` by `resolveStackCollection`'s rule (the top level, or each package body for a multi-package stack) off the stack and off each app bundle already in `plugins`. Each page is judged by `defaultRecordPageObject` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`), the reading the registration refusal uses.
- **The remedy sentence (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`).** "...or compose the deployment without the package that ships the other" now reads "...or compose the deployment without the other package's page". It names no option, no package and no tracker number. The code, the `422` status, the named pages and the first sentence are unchanged.
- ⛔ No precedence ladder and ⛔ no registration-order rule. The answer is one yes/no on a declared fact and does not depend on plugin order. A second default the app or any other package brings is still refused by the registry, naming both pages.

## Derive vs forward (the measurement)

| question | derive | forward |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Does the root have the app's pages before `new AuthPlugin(...)`? | **yes.** `serve.ts` has `config` in scope and has already appended `new AppPlugin(config)` to `plugins` (step 3, before step 5d). `DevPlugin` has `this.options.stack`. | n/a |
| New authorable surface | none | a spec key, its liveness row, docs, generated baselines |
| Can the author get it wrong? | No. The declaration is the switch. | Yes. An author who ships the page and forgets the key is still refused at boot, and a key set with no page silently drops the Members / Invitations / Teams tabs. |
| Is it a single yes/no on a declared fact? | yes (`defaultRecordPageObject(page) === 'sys_organization'` over the app's pages) | n/a |

Derive was reachable cleanly from both roots, so forward was not built.

**Where the predicate lives.** In `@objectstack/core`: `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/plugin-dev` both depend on it, and neither can import the other. Core already hosts `resolveStackCollection` and the auth-family gate `resolvePlatformAuthComposition` for the same reason. Core already depends on `@objectstack/spec`, so nothing points the wrong way. It is a new file rather than an addition to `stack-auth.ts`, because that module's header promises "importing this module loads nothing", and this one imports `@objectstack/spec/ui`.

**File surface vs the claim.** The claim names `serve.ts`, `dev-plugin.ts`, `registry.ts`, their tests and the changeset. Two further paths:
- `packages/core/src/{stack-organization-record-page.ts,index.ts}` and the predicate's test hold the shared predicate. The dispatch asked for one predicate shared by both roots.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/boot-preparation-parity.test.ts` gains one `SERVE_ONLY` row. That pin reds when `serve.ts` uses a core function that `os migrate`'s one-shot boot does not. The reason recorded in the row: the migrate boot composes `plugin-auth`'s objects through `createIdentityObjectsPlugin`, which registers no page, so it has no organization page to leave out.

## Pins (each with a negative control)

- **`packages/cli/test/serve-organization-record-page.e2e.test.ts`, a real `os serve`.** It boots a `defineStack` app, signs in as the seeded dev admin and reads `GET /api/v1/meta/page`.
  1. The app declares `orgpage_organization_detail` as the `sys_organization` default. The boot reaches its banner with no conflict, and the `sys_organization` defaults are exactly `["orgpage_organization_detail of com.example.orgpage"]`.
  2. Control: the same app without the page. The defaults are exactly `["sys_organization_detail of com.objectstack.plugin-auth"]`, so the reading in case 1 is not vacuous.
  - Both cases also read `sys_user` = `["sys_user_detail of com.objectstack.plugin-auth"]`: the option removes exactly one page.
  - It is in the nightly `e2e` tier, by name. Two `os serve` boots take about 28 s, so per-PR CI runs the contract pin below instead.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/serve-auth-organization-record-page.contract.test.ts` (unit tier, per PR).** The single `new AuthPlugin(` literal in `serve.ts` (comments masked, as `serve-auth-app-name.contract.test.ts` reads it) passes `registerOrganizationRecordPage: !stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(config, plugins)`. The predicate reads an AppPlugin-shaped bundle, with an `isDefault: false` control.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin-organization-record-page.test.ts`.** `DevPlugin.init()` with a recording `AuthPlugin`: the app page gives `false`. Controls: the same page with `isDefault: false`, no pages, and no stack each give `true`.
- **`packages/core/src/stack-organization-record-page.test.ts`.** 11 cases. Yes: top-level pages, an untyped page (a record page by default), a page in a `packages[]` body, an app plugin's `bundle`. No: `isDefault: false` or absent, another object, a `home` page, an empty stack, a body or bundle without the default.
- **`packages/objectql/src/registry-default-record-page.test.ts`**, new case: `code` + `status` (`DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` / `422`), and the remedy sentence asserted verbatim: "Keep one default per object: set `isDefault: false` on one of the two pages, or compose the deployment without the other package's page". The message contains neither "without the package" nor an option name, a package name or a `#NNN`.
- **Pin sweep.** I grepped the old sentence and `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` repo-wide, examples included. No test pinned the remedy text: the existing pins read only the first sentence, `split('. ')[0]`, and stay verbatim. The other hits are prose; see Acceptance notes.

**Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, under `os-verify-lock`, each restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty):

| mutation | anchor | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `serve.ts`: the derived option replaced by `registerOrganizationRecordPage: true,` | x1 to x0, blob `e06e62ff1b24` to `6bd5bb650dd5` | e2e case 1 **red**: `os serve ... exited 1 before /Press Ctrl\+C to stop/`, with the child printing `✗ Default record page conflict: page "orgpage_organization_detail" of package "com.example.orgpage" cannot be the default record page of object "sys_organization": page "sys_organization_detail" of package "com.objectstack.plugin-auth" already is. Keep one default per object: ... or compose the deployment without the other package's page.` The control stays green. 1 failed, 1 passed. |
| `dev-plugin.ts`: the same mutation | x1 to x0, blob `55c505e1c936` to `20335a650c35` | the app-page case **red**, the 2 controls green |
| `registry.ts`: the old remedy text restored | x1 to x0, blob `8fb229d5bace` to `7da871a01cc3` | the new remedy case **red**, 17 others green |

`serve.ts` runs from `src/` through tsx (`bin/run-dev.js`). The plugin-dev and objectql tests import their subject relatively. So none of the three mutated subjects resolves through a `dist/`.

## Verification

Head `c2db30e787` (`origin/main` `5fd2c76d6` merged in, a plain merge with no generated artifacts on either side), after a full `turbo run build` (76/76 tasks). All readings are on a shared box.

- **Derived gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **77** commands from the 12-path change set. All 77 ran, each exit code captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reconciled `77 derived, 77 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
  - `check:type-check-debt` exited 3 in the battery (`queue-timeout`, never acquired). It was re-run under the lock as its refusal prescribes: `none above its recorded number`, exit 0.
  - Pre-merge, `check-engine-split-ratio` refused on the shallow clone (exit 2). It read 98.5% after `fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-09`. The `dual-build` and `i18n` gates exited 3 (unbuilt CLI). All three pass on the merged, built head.
- **Tests on the merged head:**
  - `@objectstack/core` `stack-organization-record-page.test.ts`: 11 passed.
  - `@objectstack/objectql` default-record-page registry and save-door tests: 38 passed.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-dev` full suite: 10 files, 89 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/cli` unit: the contract pin, `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts` and `vitest-tiers-partition.test.ts`: 61 passed.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `organization-record-page-option.test.ts`: 3 passed.
  - The e2e above: 2 passed, 27.9 s.
  - `@objectstack/spec` `test:repo`: 61 files, 1033 tests passed.
- **Full suites before the merge** (at `7c4bce2697`, before the merge. The merge changed no source file of these packages; it did change `packages/spec`, whose `test:repo` and the targeted suites above re-ran green on the merged head, and the full suites were not re-run):
  - `@objectstack/core`: 99 files, 2452 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/objectql`: 418 files, 8109 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/cli --project unit`: 288 passed, 1 failed. The failure was `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts` naming `stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage`, fixed in `891cc1736` and green above.
  - The `integration` tier is declared to CI; the only spawn file this diff adds is the e2e above, run locally.
- **Typecheck:** `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-dev`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/cli` all exit 0. Every `check:test-typecheck` is OK with no new ledger entries.
- **Lint, a proven narrowing:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 11 changed `.ts` files reports 11 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings, and none reported as ignored. The repo config has no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (type-aware linting is off), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **The save door's remedy names the same untakeable step.** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s `saveMetaItem` refusal (`protocol.ts`, the `remedy` built beside `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT`) says "a page a package ships stays the default unless the deployment is composed without that package". It is the same family as this card's second half, in a file outside this claim. Its reach through a public door was not measured. Successor: none.
- **The spec docblock carries the old sentence too.** `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts`, `PageSchema.isDefault` TSDoc: "compose the deployment without the package that ships the other". This is author-facing prose, not runtime text, and `packages/spec` is outside this claim, so it is unchanged. Successor: none.
- `.changeset/pre/23015-one-default-record-page-per-object.md` keeps the old wording. It is a pre-mode release record and not this PR's to edit.
- `plugin-auth`'s README still shows the option set by hand. That stays correct for a host that composes its own kernel; under `os serve` and `DevPlugin` it is now derived.
- A malformed `packages` on an option-B stack that carries no top-level `pages` makes the predicate raise the collection reader's `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES`. That is the refusal the same boot raises when it registers that stack, and it is not swallowed here.
